To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IL-4 suppresses the biosynthesis of metalloprotein by human alveolar and peripheral blood macrophages.
IL-4 suppresses macrophage metaloproteinase expression and may thus play a role in the regulation of extracellular matrix degradation in the lung.
IL-4, but not IL-2, suppresses macrophage production and release of the metalloproteinases interstitial collagenase, 92-kD collagenase (gelatinase B), and 72-kD collagenase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of metalloprotein-ase production in human mononuclear phage cells.
the role of cytokines in the regulation of extracellular matrix degradation by macrophages.
the role of macrophages and lymphocytes in the regulation of matrix degradation in human alveoli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IL-4 is a potent inhibitor of monocyte metalloproteinase release, whereas IFN-gamma suppresses the production of both enzymes and TIMP.

the addition of IL-1, TNF alpha, IL-2, and IFN gamma to macrophages stimulated by S. aureus or IL-4 to unstimulated macrophages, results in an increase in the production of collagenase and 94 kDa enzyme.
the addition of IL-6 had minimal effects on macrophage production, whereas IL-6 specifically augmented TIMP release.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cytokine milieu within the inflammatory lesion can profoundly affect the ability of the macrophages to degrade matrix.
IL-4 is a powerful inhibitor of macrophage metaloproteinases.
IL-4 and GM-CSF suppress metalloproteinase release, whereas IFN-gamma and TNF alpha stimulate metalloproteinase secretion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL-4 and IL-6 are the only T cell products that we have found to affect metalloproteinase release by monocytes.
IL-4, which is produced by T helper type 2 lymphocytes, suppresses the release of matrix metalloproteinase by human alveolar and blood monocyte/macrophages.
the macrophage is a highly regulated cell that responds to a variety of cytokines.
